title: Stalks of the pushforward of a module along a closed immersion
statement: Let $i:Z\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] whose underlying continuous map is a homeomorphism of $Z$ onto a closed subset $i(Z)\subseteq X$ (for instance a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]), with stalk maps $i^\sharp_z:\mathcal O_{X,i(z)}\to\mathcal O_{Z,z}$. Let $\mathcal G$ be an $\mathcal O_Z$-module and $i_*\mathcal G$ its pushforward, $(i_*\mathcal G)(V)=\mathcal G(i^{-1}V)$ for $V\subseteq X$ open [def-pc-module-pullback]; stalks and germs are as in [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. (1) For every $x\in X\setminus i(Z)$ the stalk $(i_*\mathcal G)_x$ is $0$. (2) For every $z\in Z$ the map $c_z:(i_*\mathcal G)_{i(z)}\to\mathcal G_z$, $s_{i(z)}\mapsto s_z$ (for $V\ni i(z)$ open and $s\in(i_*\mathcal G)(V)=\mathcal G(i^{-1}V)$) is well defined and bijective, and it is $\mathcal O_{X,i(z)}$-linear when $\mathcal G_z$ is regarded as an $\mathcal O_{X,i(z)}$-module through $i^\sharp_z$; $c_z$ is natural in $\mathcal G$.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 00AE (sheaves-lemma-stalks-closed-pushforward), stated there for the inclusion of a closed subset and for sheaves of sets, abelian groups or algebraic structures; the linearity over O_{X,i(z)} is the germ computation used in the proof of Modules, Lemma 08KS (modules-lemma-i-star-equivalence), literature/stacks-project/modules.tex

proof.text: *Pushforward sections and stalk notation.* By [def-pc-module-pullback], for every open V subset X the pushforward is (i_* G)(V) = G(i^{-1} V), and its restriction maps are those of G. Thus a germ in (i_* G)_x is represented by a section s in G(i^{-1} V) for an open neighbourhood V of x, while a germ in G_z is represented by the same section on an open neighbourhood of z [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. The map c_z in the statement is therefore the map induced by sending this representative to its germ at z.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 00AE, setup and definition of i_*

proof.text: *Vanishing off the image.* If x is not in the closed subset i(Z), then X \ i(Z) is an open neighbourhood of x. Taking V = X \ i(Z), one has i^{-1} V = emptyset. The sections of an O_Z-module over the empty open are the zero module, so (i_* G)(V) = 0. Every germ at x is represented after restriction to this neighbourhood, hence (i_* G)_x = 0 by [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk].

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 00AE, proof: if x notin Z choose arbitrarily small U disjoint from Z; F(i^{-1}U) is the final object (zero for abelian sheaves)

proof.text: *Neighbourhoods over a point of Z.* Fix z in Z and x = i(z). Since i identifies Z homeomorphically with the closed subspace i(Z), the sets i^{-1}V, as V ranges over open neighbourhoods of x in X, form a cofinal neighbourhood basis of z in Z: for every open W containing z in Z, write W = Z intersect U for an open U in X and replace U by U union (X \ i(Z)) to obtain V with x in V and i^{-1}V = W. Conversely, i^{-1}V is an open neighbourhood of z. This is exactly the neighbourhood observation in the proof of Stacks Lemma 00AE.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 00AE, proof: every neighbourhood of z in Z is Z cap U for an open U of X

proof.text: *The stalk map is bijective.* By the preceding cofinality, the directed colimit defining (i_* G)_x is the colimit of G(i^{-1}V) over the same neighbourhood system as the colimit defining G_z. Under this identification, the canonical map sends the class of s in G(i^{-1}V) to the class of the same s in G_z, hence is c_z. It is well defined because equality of germs means equality after restriction on a smaller neighbourhood [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], and it is bijective because the two colimits have cofinal indexing systems. This is the second case of Stacks Lemma 00AE.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 00AE, proof: the second case follows because every neighbourhood of z is Z cap U; canonical map is an isomorphism on stalks

proof.text: *Linearity.* For a_x in O_{X,x} represented by a section a on V and s_{i(z)} represented by s in G(i^{-1}V), the pushforward module structure gives a_x s_{i(z)} = (a|_{i^{-1}V} s)_{i(z)}. Applying c_z gives (a|_{i^{-1}V} s)_z = i^sharp_z(a_x) s_z by the germ multiplication rule in [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Thus c_z is O_{X,i(z)}-linear for the action through i^sharp_z.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 08KS, stalk computation for i_* and O_X-linearity; the germ multiplication is the module-stalk construction

proof.text: *Naturality.* For a morphism of O_Z-modules phi: G -> H, the map on pushforwards sends a representative s in G(i^{-1}V) to phi(s) in H(i^{-1}V), and the induced stalk maps send s_z to phi(s)_z. Therefore c_z,H composed with (i_* phi)_x equals phi_z composed with c_z,G on every germ representative, so the square commutes and c_z is natural in G.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 00AE, canonical identification on stalks; naturality follows from functoriality of germs

proof_origin.place: Sheaves, Lemma 00AE (sheaves-lemma-stalks-closed-pushforward), proof; O_X-linearity follows the stalk computation used in Modules, Lemma 08KS
